newsitem.title: USA: Egypt gene order not for shipments underway -USDA.
newsitem.headline: Egypt gene order not for shipments underway -USDA.

text.p: U.S. Agriculture Department officials said Monday an Egyptian decree requiring proof grain imports have not been genetically altered does not affect shipments already underway at the time the order was issued.

USDA officials held meetings Sunday in Cairo with Egyptian government officials about the unforseen decree and expect to meet frequently over the next few days, said USDA General Sales Manager Chris Goldthwait.

"We do not yet have an ultimate resolution of the problem but it does seem as if the Egyptians want to work with us and be as flexible as they can be with respect to vessels that are either on the water or in the process of loading," he said.
"It is possible as we talk over the next couple of days there may be some further relaxation," Goldthwait added.

The Egyptian Health Ministry has issued a decree that it will require imports of commodities meant for human consumption to be accompanied by proof that genetic engineering was not used in their production. The news seeped out last week after traders were given a copy of the order, dated July 1.
Goldthwait said the order does not pertain to animal feed.
Egypt was the No. 2 purchaser of U.S. wheat after Japan last year. There is no genetically altered wheat on the market. Goldthwait said the decree should not affect wheat shipments.
Egypt is also a big customer of U.S. corn, which has been heavily planted to gene-altered seed this year.
Goldthwait said U.S. officials were trying to get the decree clarified.
"We need another day or two whether we can say if it's a serious problem," he said. "The initial feedback we got after meetings yesterday was somewhat encouraging."
